This is a petition under Section 528 of Bnss for quashing of the Fir No.136 dated 15.05.2018
(Annexure P-1) registered under Section 174-A of Ipc, at Police Station Civil Line Sonipat, District
Sonipat, Haryana which was registered consequent to the order dated 21.03.2018 (Annexure P-2)
passed by the Acjm, Sonepat declaring the petitioner as a proclaimed person.

2.  The brief facts of the case are that COMI/6045/2013 dated 06.09.2021 U/s 406, 417, 420, 465,
468, 469, 506 IPC, P.S. Civil Line, District Sonipat came to be registered against the petitioner.

The petitioner was declared a proclaimed person vide order dated 21.03.2018 (Annexure P-2) and directions were issued to the concerned Police Station for registration of an FIR under Section 174A IPC.

Subsequent thereto, the FIR came to be registered under Section 174A IPC on 15.05.2018 (P-1).
3.
It is this FIR which is under challenge in the present petition.

The learned counsel for the petitioner/accused submits that he had wrongly been declared a proclaimed person and on learning about the same, the petitioner compromised the matter with the complainant/respondent No.2.

Thereafter, on 06.09.2021, the counsel for respondent No.2-complainant in the Trial Court got recorded his statement that as per his instructions, the complainant did not want to proceed further with the present complaint and wanted to withdraw the same.
Based on the said statement, the complaint was ordered to be dismissed as withdrawn on 06.09.2021.

The copy of the order dated 06.09.2021 is marked as X.
5.
The learned State counsel has opposed the present petition and has submitted that the proclamation order has rightly been passed.

6. This Court has heard the learned counsel for the parties and has perused the paper-book..
7.

From the above-said facts and circumstances, it is apparent that the present FIR was registered in view of the fact that the petitioner was declared as a proclaimed person in COMI/6045/2013 dated 06.09.2021 U/s 406, 417, 420, 465, 468, 469, 506 IPC, P.S. Civil Line, District Sonipat.

8. A co-ordinate Bench of this Court in CRM-M-43813-2018 titled as "Baldev Chand Bansal vs. State of Haryana and another", decided on 29.01.2019 has held as under:-
"Prayer in this petition is for quashing of FIR No.64 dated 15.02.2017 filed under Section 174-A of the Indian Penal Code registered at Police Station Sector-5,
Panchkula and all other subsequent proceedings arising thereof as well as order dated 24.10.2016 passed by the trial Court vide which a direction was issued to register the aforesaid FIR.

State of Haryana and another, 2015 (32) RCR (Crl.) 790 and "Rajneesh Khanna Vs.

sentences.text: A perusal of the above judgment would show that in a similar case where the FIR had been registered under Section 174-A IPC in view of the order passed in proceedings under Section 138 of the Negotiable Instruments Act, while declaring the petitioner therein as a proclaimed offender, a co-ordinate Bench after relying upon various judgments 3 of 5 CRM-M-6256-2026 observed that once the main petition under Section 138 of the Negotiable Instruments Act stands withdrawn in view of an amicable settlement between the parties, the continuation of proceedings under Section 174-A IPC is nothing but an abuse of the process of law.

The said aspect was one of the main considerations for allowing the petition and setting aside the order declaring the petitioner therein as a proclaimed person as well as quashing of the FIR under Section 174-A IPC.

Another co-ordinate Bench of this Court in a case titled as "Ashok Madan vs. State of Haryana and another" reported as 2020(4) RCR (Criminal) 87 has also held as under:-
"No doubt, the learned counsel for the respondent has vehemently argued that the offence under Section 174A I.P.C. is independent of the main case, therefore, merely because the main case has been dismissed for want of prosecution, the present petition cannot be allowed, however, keeping in view the fact that the present FIR was registered only on account of absence from the proceedings in the main case which had been subsequently regularised by the court while granting bail to the petitioner, the default stood condoned.

7. Accordingly, the petition is allowed.

FIR No.446 dated 21.08.2017, registered under Section 174A I.P.C. At Police Station Kotwali, District Faridabad, as well as consequential proceedings shall stand quashed."
4 of 5 CRM-M-6256-2026 10.

A perusal of the relevant extract of the above judgment would show that where the main case was dismissed for want of prosecution, it was observed that the continuation of proceedings under Section 174-A IPC shall be an abuse of the process of court.

A similar view has been expressed by this Court in "Anil Kumar Versus Jitender Kumar and another, CRM-M- 5878-2022 decided on 06.04.2022", "Anil Kumar Versus Jitender Kumar and another, CRM-M-5755-2022 decided on 06.04.2022" and "Varinder Kumar @ Virender Kumar Versus State of Haryana and another,
CRM-M-42551- 2021 decided on 19.04.2022".
